glm-5.3-flash on 16x h100: glm53flash-h100-chatbot-kernel-0001

A deterministic sweep over chatbot traffic, comparing 8 designs on one GPU budget.

BLIS discrete-event simulationExperiment Spec (RFC #21)deterministic sweep — no LLM in the measurement pathseed 42

What was tested

276 configurations over 8 sweeps (shape-and-ep, batch-caps-vs-shape, moe-dispatch, eplb-vs-dispatch, graph-capture, capture-size-vs-batch, prefill-admission, routing), each at 5 load levels, every run on exactly 16 GPUs.

What was found

1x TP16 + EP (graph capture full), from the graph-capture sweep, reached 88.95 tok/s/GPU (1423.3 tok/s across the fleet) at concurrency 16 while holding the scenario's SLOs.

What to run

1x TP16 + EP (graph capture full) at concurrency 16. 286 of 1380 runs held the SLOs.

1The measurements

Every run in this experiment is in the explorer below: filter by outcome to see which settings held the SLOs, or by setting to compare one sweep against another.

Each sweep's hypothesis was written before the runs, and is quoted beside that sweep's measured result below.

2Sweep: shape-and-ep

EP should pay most at tp 8 and fade as dp grows, since wider dp already splits the batch and EP adds dispatch on top.

Measured: best was 1x TP16 + EP at 85.45 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 16).

3Sweep: batch-caps-vs-shape

The sequence cap should bind well before the token cap on short chatbot prompts, and hardest on one wide instance.

Measured: best was 1x TP16 + EP (max seqs 1,024) at 85.45 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 16).

4Sweep: moe-dispatch

DeepEP backends should lose to allgather/pplx at small dp and close the gap as dp widens, where the token cap admits them.

Measured: best was 1x TP8xDP2 + EP at 79.2 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 16).

5Sweep: eplb-vs-dispatch

Redundant experts should help most at the widest dp, where an uneven expert load stalls the most ranks.

Measured: best was 2x TP4xDP2 + EP at 14.15 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 2).

6Sweep: graph-capture

Full graph capture should beat PIECEWISE by a few percent at every shape, and NONE should roughly halve throughput.

Measured: best was 1x TP16 + EP (graph capture full) at 88.95 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 16).

7Sweep: capture-size-vs-batch

A small capture size should cost throughput only when max_num_seqs lets the batch grow past it.

Measured: best was 2x TP8 + EP (graph capture full · max captured step 512) at 19.93 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 2).

8Sweep: prefill-admission

Chunking prefills below the 256-token median prompt should cut the ITL tail but cost throughput, most on one wide instance.

Measured: best was 1x TP16 + EP (batch tokens 8,192 · prefill chunk 1,024) at 85.45 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 16).

9Sweep: routing

With only two endpoints, routing should move throughput a few percent at most, slightly more when the batch cap binds.

Measured: best was 2x TP8 + EP (load-aware routing · max seqs 1,024) at 19 tok/s/GPU (concurrency 2).
